competitive_landscape: The Bali–Gili–Lombok corridor is served by fast boats with uneven safety and comfort records, and a slower public ferry (Padangbai–Lembar). Lombok is the pivot from Bali toward the eastern islands, but the onward reach to Komodo and the Sumbawa outposts has no fast premium service.

grab.note: Lombok extends the Grab Bali phase — Gili hops plus the bridge toward Komodo.

precedents.why_it_matters: Proof that clean foiling island-hopping scales — directly relevant to the Bali-to-Komodo chain.

regulatory_note: Sea transport falls under Indonesia's KSOP / Directorate of Sea Transportation, with the Mandalika SEZ (ITDC) as a development anchor — supportive of upgraded, cleaner marine links.
seasonality: The dry season (Apr–Oct) offers the best conditions; the wet season (Nov–Mar) brings rougher seas. The Lombok Strait runs strong currents and swell that foiling rides far better than conventional fast boats.

summary: Lombok is the pivot of the hero island-hopping chain: the Gili islands and Mandalika draw high day-trip volumes close in, while Lombok is the natural stepping-stone from Bali toward Komodo and Sumba. Pioneer II handles the Gili and Bali-Lombok hops; Quanta-LR carries the longer reach toward Komodo.
tagline: The first link out of Bali — Gilis, Mandalika, and the bridge to Komodo.
transit_planning: For an operator: a premium water tier relieving the crowded Gili fast-boat corridor and forming the central pivot of the Bali → Lombok → Komodo → Sumba luxury chain.
